registry.description: Bitterness is the taste of prolonged hurt turned inward — the inner residue of unresolved grief, injustice, or loss that has curdled into a permanent sourness of soul. The Hebrew vocabulary draws directly on the physical sensation of bitter taste, and the Greek carries this metaphor into the New Testament: a root of bitterness that grows and defiles many. Bitterness is not just sadness; it is sorrow that has calcified into resentment, a hardening of the inner person against the possibility of healing.

terms.medium_def:
1) to be leavened, be sour
1a) (Qal) to be leavened
1b) (Hiphil) to taste something leavened
1c) (Hithpael) to be embittered, grieved
